title: Masala Omelette, Anda Bhurji Make TasteAtlas 50 Best Egg Dishes
excerpt: India's two breakfast staples placed 20th and 35th on TasteAtlas's world egg-dish rankings, behind Japan's ajitsuke tamago at No. 1.
body:
• Masala omelette placed 20th and anda bhurji 35th on TasteAtlas's ranking of the world's best egg dishes, in the list current to November 15, 2026.
  • Japan's ajitsuke tamago — soft-boiled eggs soaked in mirin and soy sauce — took the No. 1 spot, ahead of Greece's strapatsada and Spain's tortilla de Betanzos.
  • TasteAtlas rates the masala omelet 4.1 and anda bhurji 3.9 on its India egg-dishes list. Both are breakfast dishes: the omelette whisked with onion, chillies and spices, the bhurji a spicy scramble with tomato and onion.
  • The rankings are audience ratings, not judges' scores: TasteAtlas recorded 10,922 ratings for the world list, of which 7,273 were recognised as legitimate, and the guide itself says its rankings should not be seen as a final global conclusion.

Two dishes that start the day in millions of Indian homes have made a global list. TasteAtlas, the food and travel guide, places India's masala omelette at No. 20 and anda bhurji at No. 35 on its ranking of the best egg dishes in the world, in the list current to November 15, 2026, as reported by Curly Tales.

The two Indian entries

The masala omelet is a traditional egg dish that TasteAtlas describes as originating in South India. It is made with eggs, onions, green chilli peppers, coriander, chilli powder and turmeric powder; Curly Tales' account of the list adds peppers to the mix. The eggs are whisked with the other ingredients and cooked in a pan on both sides until the omelette is slightly crisp at the edges. It is traditionally a breakfast dish, served with pav.

Anda bhurji is India's spiced scrambled egg. Curly Tales describes it as made with eggs, tomatoes, onions, cumin seeds and spices; TasteAtlas calls it a traditional dish of spicy scrambled eggs. It is usually served at breakfast with toasted bread, pav or parathas. On TasteAtlas's own India egg-dishes list, the masala omelet carries a 4.1 rating and anda bhurji a 3.9.

What beat them

The No. 1 spot went to Japan's ajitsuke tamago, soft-boiled eggs soaked in mirin and soy sauce, eaten as a snack, in a bento, or most commonly as a ramen topping, with the yolks left custardy. Greece's strapatsada — tomatoes sautéed with herbs, combined with beaten eggs and topped with crumbled feta — placed second, Spain's tortilla de Betanzos third, the Philippines' tortang talong fourth and shakshouka fifth.

How the list is built

TasteAtlas rankings rest on its audience's ratings, filtered by mechanisms the guide says recognise real users and discount bot, nationalist or local patriotic ratings, with extra weight for users it recognises as knowledgeable. For the world egg-dishes list it recorded 10,922 ratings until November 15, 2026, of which 7,273 were recognised as legitimate. The guide is plain about the limits: its rankings “should not be seen as the final global conclusion about food,” and exist to promote local dishes and arouse curiosity about ones readers have not tried.

Cook the No. 20 at home

Nothing on either plate needs a specialty store, which is the point of both dishes. The masala omelette's method, as TasteAtlas records it, is the whole recipe: whisk, pour, crisp the edges, eat with pav. The card below carries the dish in the guide's own terms.
